audience_profile: Senior engineers who use CDNs but may not have looked at CloudFront's scale, Netflix's in-ISP appliances, or a real X-Cache/Age response.
learning_objective: Explain why a stream starts fast: copies near viewers (CloudFront POPs, Netflix Open Connect inside ISPs), what a miss and a hit do, and how to see it in real headers.
creative_concept: Start on the real night Earth over London, show the cost of one distant origin, light up the edge network, step inside an ISP, then prove miss and hit with a real response.

treatments.name: A. Press play, then a powers-of-ten journey to the rack, then real headers
treatments.shape: footage, wide space, regional map, city close-up, building, rack, split screen, sequence, terminal, cards
treatments.verdict: Chosen: concrete geography, sourced scale, and a proof the viewer can reproduce.

treatments.name: B. Diagram-only walkthrough
treatments.shape: iconflow and sequence for every step
treatments.verdict: Rejected: precise but static for 60 s on a phone.

treatments.name: C. Numbers-led explainer
treatments.shape: charts of latency and hit ratio
treatments.verdict: Rejected: needs figures no official page gives.

chosen: A. Press play, then a powers-of-ten journey to the rack, then real headers
hook: The channel owner's clip: a viewer presses play; the screen's last glowing point opens into the night Earth.
narrative_structure: Question; one distant origin; the CDN idea with a sourced count; the edge network lights up; Netflix Open Connect; inside the ISP; miss versus hit; steps on a miss; real response; benefits and the answer.
visual_direction: noir-network, real NASA night imagery for the globe scenes, glowing city points, arcs with light-trail packets, no decorative shapes.
narration_approach: Short sentences, real names (CloudFront, Open Connect, X-Cache, Age), us-east-1 spoken as U S East 1.

decisions.choice: Fly into London on the real night Earth with the question

User's explicit choice (override of the variety rule): matches the dark reference images.

A real curl -I response captured 2026-11-23, labelled real response with the date
decisions.reason: Never show invented lines; senior engineers can reproduce it.

decisions.choice: 9:16, captions off, one idea per scene, short end holds
decisions.reason: Vertical Reel; keeps the content inside 60 +- 5 s.

decisions.choice: Camera fly-to, light-trail packets, counter with source, split-screen, staggered build
decisions.reason: Adopted from the Scout's reading of cinelume, remocn and clapcode.

decisions.choice: One continuous camera: space, Europe, Asia, building, rack; a different shot type in every scene
decisions.reason: A journey holds attention and shows real AWS geography (Regions and edge locations from official pages).

dropoff.countermeasure: Focus frame walks one hop per spoken word

experiment: Does the real-response terminal scene hold retention better than a recap?

effects_reason: globe and flat_map for a continuous camera journey on real NASA imagery (space, Europe, Asia); model_3d for the building and the Open Connect rack; scroll_demo for the real response; stacking_cards for the benefits; parallax grid for depth behind the split screen.
